title: The Insane Story Behind the Mercedes 6x6

scenes.text: In March twenty thirteen, Mercedes showed a six-wheeled G 63 AMG and its own spokesman said there was no plan for series production. By February twenty fifteen, more than one hundred had been built and the run was sold out. In between lies an army contract, a price that moved, a production number that moved, and a pickup that Australia could not buy. This is the story, with every claim sourced.
scenes.caption: THE INSANE STORY BEHIND THE MERCEDES 6x6

scenes.text: We rely on GoAuto, Motor Authority, Autocar, CarAdvice, Wikipedia, Barrett-Jackson, MBWorld, The Classic Valuer, The Drive and Carscoops. Several of them disagree about dates, prices and numbers. Those disagreements are part of the story, so we show them. Our own arithmetic is labelled.
scenes.caption: SOURCES: GOAUTO · MOTOR AUTHORITY · AUTOCAR · CARADVICE · WIKIPEDIA · BARRETT-JACKSON · MBWORLD · THE CLASSIC VALUER · THE DRIVE · CARSCOOPS · DISAGREEMENTS ARE SHOWN · OUR ARITHMETIC IS LABELLED

scenes.text: The story starts with soldiers, not millionaires. GoAuto, on the third of November two thousand nine, reported that the Australian Defence Force had taken delivery of the first two prototypes of its new Mercedes G-Class fleet, at a ceremony at the Graz plant in Austria. The programme was called Land one two one, also known as Overlander.
scenes.caption: GOAUTO (3 NOV 2009): FIRST TWO PROTOTYPES DELIVERED AT A CEREMONY AT MERCEDES' GRAZ PLANT · PROGRAMME: LAND 121, ALSO CALLED 'OVERLANDER'

scenes.text: The scale was large. GoAuto says the contract was worth three hundred fifty million dollars, signed about twelve months before the prototypes, for twelve hundred vehicles, with a fifteen-year service and parts contract. The article does not state the currency, though it is an Australian outlet. A 2007 article it links to said eleven hundred G-Wagons.
scenes.caption: GOAUTO: $350 MILLION (CURRENCY NOT STATED) · ~1,200 VEHICLES · 15-YEAR SUPPORT CONTRACT · SIGNED ~12 MONTHS BEFORE PROTOTYPES · A 2007 ARTICLE: '1100 G-WAGONS'

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, three hundred fifty million over twelve hundred vehicles is about two hundred ninety-two thousand per vehicle. That is not a vehicle price, because the contract also covers support and modules, but it shows that this was a very large, long-term military deal. We do not have a breakdown in our sources.
scenes.caption: $350,000,000 ÷ 1,200 = $291,667 (OUR ARITHMETIC; INCLUDES 15-YEAR SUPPORT; NOT A UNIT PRICE; NO BREAKDOWN IN OUR SOURCES)

scenes.text: Among the variants were two-door and four-door 4x4 wagons, cab-chassis utilities, and purpose-built 6x6 single-cab and dual-cab chassis models. There was also a specialised 6x6 surveillance and reconnaissance version for use in northern Australia. So the six-wheeler was designed as a working military chassis from the start.
scenes.caption: GOAUTO: 4x4 WAGONS (2- AND 4-DOOR) · 4x4 CAB-CHASSIS · PURPOSE-BUILT 6x6 SINGLE- AND DUAL-CAB CHASSIS · 6x6 SURVEILLANCE / RECONNAISSANCE VERSION 'FOR USE IN NORTHERN AUSTRALIA'

scenes.text: The plan, per GoAuto, was twelve months of prototype testing, production deliveries from twenty eleven, and supply contracted until at least twenty fourteen. It called the arrangement a thirty-year strategic agreement. Newcastle-based Varley was to supply transport modules such as ambulance, command post, personnel carriage and general cargo.
scenes.caption: GOAUTO: 12 MONTHS OF TESTING · PRODUCTION DELIVERIES FROM 2011 · SUPPLY UNTIL AT LEAST 2014 · '30-YEAR STRATEGIC AGREEMENT' · VARLEY (NEWCASTLE) SUPPLIES MODULES

scenes.text: Now the date puzzle. Wikipedia says the vehicle was developed for the Australian Army from two thousand seven. Motor Authority, in March twenty thirteen, said it was first developed in twenty eleven for the Australian military, in a spec based on the diesel G 320 CDI. Those look contradictory.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: DEVELOPED FROM 2007 · MOTOR AUTHORITY (1 MAR 2013): 'FIRST DEVELOPED IN 2011' FOR THE AUSTRALIAN MILITARY, BASED ON G 320 CDI

scenes.text: GoAuto's twenty nine article may reconcile them. It shows a contract signed around late two thousand eight, prototypes in two thousand nine, and production deliveries planned from twenty eleven. So twenty eleven may be when the military six-wheelers reached service. That is our reading, not a statement in any source, and we flag it as such.
scenes.caption: GOAUTO 2009: CONTRACT ~LATE 2008 · PROTOTYPES 2009 · DELIVERIES FROM 2011 → '2011' MAY MEAN SERVICE ENTRY (OUR READING, NOT STATED IN ANY SOURCE) · 2007 DEAL ARTICLE ALSO CITED BY GOAUTO

scenes.text: The military truck did not end. CarAdvice, in April twenty fifteen, said the Australian Army's six-wheel G-Wagen chassis is different from the AMG version and will continue to be produced. So the story of the luxury 6x6 is a spin-off from a programme that was already running, not the other way round.
scenes.caption: CARADVICE (13 APR 2015): ARMY 6x6 CHASSIS 'IS DIFFERENT TO THE AMG VERSION AND WILL CONTINUE TO BE PRODUCED'

scenes.text: On the eighteenth of March twenty thirteen, GoAuto reported that Mercedes had revealed the six-wheeled G 63 AMG over the weekend as a show car. It used the rear twin drivetrain from the military 6x6 version, but the article said the show car was not entirely based on the military G-Wagon used by the Australian Army.
scenes.caption: GOAUTO (18 MAR 2013): REVEALED 'OVER THE WEEKEND' AS A SHOW CAR · USES REAR TWIN DRIVETRAIN FROM MILITARY 6x6 · 'NOT ENTIRELY BASED ON' THE ARMY G-WAGON

scenes.text: Mercedes-Benz Australia's senior communications manager, David McCarthy, was blunt. He told GoAuto there is no plan for a series production, but that if people want one, they will make them one. He also said there is nothing like it. Mercedes said buyers would need a lot of money, and gave no price.
scenes.caption: DAVID McCARTHY, MERCEDES-BENZ AUSTRALIA (GOAUTO, 18 MAR 2013): 'THERE IS NO PLAN FOR A SERIES PRODUCTION' · 'IF PEOPLE WANT ONE, THEY WILL MAKE THEM ONE' · 'THERE'S NOTHING LIKE IT' · NO PRICE GIVEN

scenes.text: Motor Authority, writing on the first of March twenty thirteen, was already more definite. It said the truck was built alongside the regular G-Class at Magna Steyr in Graz, that Mercedes had developed a civilian version after seeing enough interest, that it would go on sale in October, and that Mercedes predicted twenty to thirty units a year.
scenes.caption: MOTOR AUTHORITY (1 MAR 2013): BUILT AT MAGNA STEYR, GRAZ · CIVILIAN VERSION DEVELOPED 'AFTER SEEING ENOUGH INTEREST' · ON SALE IN OCTOBER · PREDICTED 20–30 UNITS A YEAR

scenes.text: So within seventeen days the story had two versions. By our arithmetic, one source on the first of March said sales in October with twenty to thirty a year, and another on the eighteenth said no plan for series production. We cannot tell from our sources whether it was a change of plan, or two different ways of describing the same small run.
scenes.caption: 1 MAR 2013: SALES FROM OCTOBER, 20–30/YEAR (MOTOR AUTHORITY) · 18 MAR 2013: 'NO PLAN FOR A SERIES PRODUCTION' (GOAUTO) · 17 DAYS APART (OUR ARITHMETIC) · REASON: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: The show car's numbers, per GoAuto: a twin-turbo V8 making four hundred kilowatts and seven hundred sixty newton-metres, five differential locks, and a tyre-pressure system for thirty-seven inch tyres. It listed a weight of 3.85 tonnes, a height of twenty-three hundred millimetres and fifteen different spring rates. Reinforced springs came from an armoured special-protection vehicle.
scenes.caption: GOAUTO: 400 KW / 760 N·M · FIVE DIFF LOCKS · 37-IN TYRES · 3.85 T · 2,300 MM HIGH · 15 SPRING RATES · FRONT AXLE USES REINFORCED SPRINGS FROM AN ARMOURED SPECIAL-PROTECTION VEHICLE

scenes.text: Compare with the later figures. By our arithmetic, Wikipedia's four thousand eighty-three kilograms is six percent heavier than the show car's 3.85 tonnes, and its height of twenty-two ten is four percent below twenty-three hundred. Motor Authority gave a curb weight of eight thousand three hundred twenty-two pounds. The specification moved between the show car and the production truck.
scenes.caption: 4,083 KG ÷ 3,850 KG = +6.0% · 2,210 MM vs 2,300 MM = −3.9% (OUR ARITHMETIC; WIKIPEDIA vs GOAUTO) · MOTOR AUTHORITY: 8,322 LB

scenes.text: Motor Authority adds that the ground clearance is eighteen point one inches, which is nine point eight inches higher than the stock G 63 AMG, and that the maximum payload is fourteen hundred thirty-three pounds. By our arithmetic, the stock truck's clearance would be eight point three inches, and the payload about six hundred fifty kilograms. The cargo bed floor is polished bamboo.
scenes.caption: MOTOR AUTHORITY: 18.1 IN CLEARANCE, 9.8 IN HIGHER THAN STOCK G63 AMG · PAYLOAD 1,433 LB · 18.1 − 9.8 = 8.3 IN STOCK · 1,433 LB = 650 KG (OUR ARITHMETIC) · BAMBOO CARGO FLOOR

scenes.text: Price is the second moving part. In March twenty thirteen, Motor Authority said Axel Harries, the G-Class development head, indicated buyers should expect no more than the sticker of the SLS AMG Electric Drive, which it gave as three hundred fifty thousand euros, about four hundred fifty-seven thousand dollars. Fox News, citing Autocar, said the same ranking.
scenes.caption: MOTOR AUTHORITY (1 MAR 2013): HARRIES INDICATED NO MORE THAN SLS AMG ELECTRIC DRIVE: €350,000 (~$457,000) · FOX NEWS (4 MAR 2013, CITING AUTOCAR): SECOND ONLY TO THE ELECTRIC AMG

scenes.text: By September, GoAuto, citing Autocar, said the car would sell from about four hundred fifty thousand euros, which it converted to six hundred fifty thousand Australian dollars, with sales starting the following month. By our arithmetic, that is twenty-nine percent above the March guidance of three hundred fifty thousand euros.
scenes.caption: GOAUTO (27 SEPT 2013, CITING AUTOCAR): FROM ~€450,000 (~A$650,000) · €450,000 ÷ €350,000 = +28.6% (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: The reported launch price was lower. CarAdvice and Carscoops say three hundred seventy-nine thousand euros. By our arithmetic, that is eight percent above the March guidance and sixteen percent below the September figure. Autocar's own review in February twenty fourteen listed three hundred seventy thousand pounds, so even Autocar's numbers differ between currencies and dates.
scenes.caption: €379,000 (CARADVICE, CARSCOOPS) · +8.3% vs €350,000 · −15.8% vs €450,000 (OUR ARITHMETIC) · AUTOCAR REVIEW (23 FEB 2014): £370,000

scenes.text: Why the numbers moved, our sources do not say. Perhaps the early figures were guidance, and the later ones were real quotes. That is our reading. What the record shows is a luxury product whose price was set late and reported with several different numbers. It was also priced above any other Mercedes except the electric SLS.
scenes.caption: REASON FOR THE CHANGES: NOT IN OUR SOURCES · 'GUIDANCE vs QUOTE' = OUR READING · WIKIPEDIA: 2ND MOST EXPENSIVE STREET-LEGAL MERCEDES AT LAUNCH

scenes.text: Production moved even more. GoAuto in September twenty thirteen said just thirty units were confirmed for production. That is up from a show car with no series plans in March, and from twenty to thirty a year predicted by Motor Authority. Then the actual run grew beyond all of that, and the truck sold out.
scenes.caption: GOAUTO (27 SEPT 2013): 'JUST 30 UNITS CONFIRMED FOR PRODUCTION' · MARCH 2013: SHOW CAR, NO SERIES PLAN · 20–30/YEAR PREDICTED (MOTOR AUTHORITY)

scenes.text: Motor Authority, on the twentieth of February twenty fifteen, reported that over one hundred examples were produced, citing GT Spirit. It also said Mercedes initially said two had been built, and that a few more could be produced pending demand. That is the writer's paraphrase of an earlier company line, not a direct quote.
scenes.caption: MOTOR AUTHORITY (20 FEB 2015, CITING GT SPIRIT 17 FEB 2015): 'OVER 100 EXAMPLES WERE PRODUCED' · MERCEDES 'INITIALLY SAID TWO HAD BEEN BUILT… A FEW MORE… PENDING DEMAND' (WRITER'S PARAPHRASE)

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, over a hundred is more than three times the thirty confirmed in September twenty thirteen, and more than three times what you get from one year of the predicted twenty to thirty. Wikipedia says Mercedes sold more units than originally anticipated. CarAdvice says the run sold out in about twelve months.
scenes.caption: 100 ÷ 30 = 3.3× THE SEPT 2013 FIGURE (OUR ARITHMETIC) · WIKIPEDIA: 'MORE UNITS… THAN ORIGINALLY ANTICIPATED' · CARADVICE: SOLD OUT IN ~12 MONTHS

scenes.text: The last stages are dated. Motor Authority's report came on the twentieth of February twenty fifteen, CarAdvice's on the thirteenth of April saying production ends that week, and Wikipedia says the last customer delivery left Graz in May twenty fifteen. By our arithmetic, from the October twenty thirteen sale start to May twenty fifteen is about nineteen months.
scenes.caption: MOTOR AUTHORITY 20 FEB 2015 · CARADVICE 13 APR 2015: PRODUCTION ENDING 'THIS WEEK' · WIKIPEDIA: LAST DELIVERY MAY 2015 · OCT 2013 → MAY 2015 ≈ 19 MONTHS (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Motor Authority also reported that Mercedes was expected to unveil a G 550 4x4 squared at the upcoming Geneva Motor Show. That was an expectation, not an announcement. Wikipedia later says the G 500 4x4 squared used the body of the long-wheelbase wagon on a shortened chassis from the 6x6. So the run ended as its successor appeared.
scenes.caption: MOTOR AUTHORITY (20 FEB 2015): G550 4x4² EXPECTED AT GENEVA (EXPECTATION, NOT ANNOUNCEMENT) · WIKIPEDIA: G 500 4x4² = LONG-WHEELBASE 5-DOOR BODY ON SHORTENED CHASSIS FROM THE 6x6

scenes.text: Here is the irony. The truck borrowed from a vehicle built for Australia's army. Yet GoAuto, on the twenty-seventh of September twenty thirteen, reported that Mercedes-Benz Australia had ruled it out. The article said it would be produced only in small numbers and, more importantly, only in left-hand drive, which scuppered any chance of local orders.
scenes.caption: GOAUTO (27 SEPT 2013): 'ONLY IN LEFT-HAND DRIVE… HAS SCUPPERED ANY POSSIBILITY OF LOCAL ORDERS' · TRUCK BORROWS PARTS FROM A VEHICLE BUILT FOR THE AUSTRALIAN ARMY
scenes.chapter: The truck Australia could not buy

scenes.text: The same outlet had quoted McCarthy in March saying there was a chance cashed-up Australian buyers could order it. By September the answer was no. Later, Wikipedia says fifteen right-hand-drive units went to Malaysia, and a South African businessman ordered ten units, converted to right-hand drive, so right-hand drive did eventually happen.
scenes.caption: GOAUTO MARCH 2013: McCARTHY — 'A CHANCE' AUSTRALIAN BUYERS COULD ORDER · SEPT 2013: LHD ONLY · WIKIPEDIA: 15 RHD UNITS FOR MALAYSIA (NAZA WORLD) · 10 UNITS CONVERTED TO RHD FOR A SOUTH AFRICAN BUSINESSMAN

scenes.text: Why not Australia then? Wikipedia says the South African buyer's units were converted after the company required a larger order before converting one. By our arithmetic, that suggests a threshold of orders was needed. Our sources do not say what the threshold was, or whether any Australian buyer asked.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: SOUTH AFRICAN BUYER ORDERED 10; 'COMPANY REQUIRED A LARGER ORDER BEFORE CONVERTING ONE' · THRESHOLD SIZE AND ANY AUSTRALIAN ORDER: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: Mercedes never sold the 6x6 new in the United States, according to MBWorld and The Drive. Cars arrived under the Show or Display exemption, with limited road use, and conversions such as those by G and K Automotive in Santa Ana. The Drive reports one car came from Japan, with about forty-nine thousand miles.
scenes.caption: MBWORLD: NOT SOLD NEW IN THE U.S., BROUGHT IN UNDER SHOW AND DISPLAY · THE DRIVE: JAPAN-DELIVERED CAR, G&K CONVERSION · ~48,990 MI
scenes.chapter: An odd place to end up: America

scenes.text: The Drive reported a sale for nine hundred one thousand, three hundred thirty-seven dollars in November twenty twenty. MercedesBlog reported a Brabus-tuned car at one million, one hundred seventy thousand in May twenty twenty-two. MBWorld reports one million, four hundred thousand dollars at Barrett-Jackson Scottsdale for a five-year-old car with nine hundred sixty-five miles, without a date.
scenes.caption: THE DRIVE (NOV 2020): $901,337 · MERCEDESBLOG (MAY 2022): $1,170,000 (BRABUS) · MBWORLD (UNDATED): $1.4 MILLION, 965 MI, BARRETT-JACKSON SCOTTSDALE, 'FIVE-YEAR-OLD' CAR

scenes.text: In January twenty twenty-five, Barrett-Jackson offered lot fourteen oh four, a two thousand fourteen car, at no reserve. Its listing describes input from AMG, a Weistec Engineering upgrade with enhanced turbochargers, and thirty-seven inch Pro Comp tyres on eighteen inch beadlock wheels. The odometer showed five thousand, four hundred seventy-one miles.
scenes.caption: BARRETT-JACKSON (26 DEC 2024): LOT 1404, 2014 G63 AMG 6x6, NO RESERVE, SCOTTSDALE JAN 2025 · WEISTEC UPGRADES · 37-IN PRO COMP EXTREME MT2 ON 18-IN BEADLOCKS · 5,471 MI

scenes.text: The Classic Valuer lists a sale of six hundred two thousand and forty-six pounds, on the twenty-sixth of January twenty twenty-five, which it says is in the bottom half of sold prices for the model. Its comparable sales since twenty twenty range from about one hundred fifty-eight thousand to eight hundred ninety-eight thousand pounds, with a median of about six hundred fifteen thousand.
scenes.caption: THE CLASSIC VALUER: £602,046 · 26 JAN 2025 · 'BOTTOM 50%' · COMPS SINCE 2020: LOW £158,417 · MEDIAN £614,655 · HIGH £897,703 · CONDITION 7/10 · CURRENCY AND IDENTIFICATION OF THE SAME CAR: NOT CONFIRMED

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, six hundred two thousand is two percent below that median. That is a very different picture from the million-dollar sales of twenty twenty-one and twenty twenty-two. We caution that the sources mix pounds and dollars, different cars, and different modifications, and the lowest comp of about one hundred fifty-eight thousand pounds is not explained.
scenes.caption: £602,046 ÷ £614,655 = −2.1% BELOW MEDIAN (OUR ARITHMETIC) · SOURCES MIX GBP / USD, MODIFIED AND STOCK CARS · LOW COMP £158,417 UNEXPLAINED

scenes.text: Barrett-Jackson's listing describes the project in the spirit of because we can, and says the 6x6 was a luxury, high-performance vehicle with input from AMG. Wikipedia says it appeared in Beyond the Reach, in twenty fourteen, and Jurassic World, in twenty fifteen. It also became the basis for the G 500 4x4 squared's chassis and for portal axles on later vehicles.
scenes.caption: BARRETT-JACKSON: SPIRIT OF 'BECAUSE WE CAN' · WIKIPEDIA: 'BEYOND THE REACH' (2014), 'JURASSIC WORLD' (2015) · PORTAL AXLES LATER USED ON G 550 4x4² (ROAD & TRACK)

scenes.text: The Hennessey VelociRaptor 6x6, first reported in October twenty sixteen, was framed by Digital Trends as a rival to the Mercedes. By our arithmetic, that came about seventeen months after Mercedes ended production. Hennessey planned fifty for the twenty eighteen model year, and started at three hundred forty-nine thousand dollars, per Motor Authority.
scenes.caption: DIGITAL TRENDS: MERCEDES NAMED AS A RIVAL · THE DRIVE 5 OCT 2016 · MOTOR AUTHORITY: 50 PLANNED FOR MY2018, FROM $349,000 · MAY 2015 → OCT 2016 ≈ 17 MONTHS (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: And the Mercedes-Maybach G 650 Landaulet, shown at Geneva in March twenty seventeen, used portal axles and raised suspension from the G 500 4x4 squared, according to Wikipedia. It was limited to ninety-nine units at seven hundred forty-nine thousand, seven hundred euros. So a vehicle born from an army contract helped shape a very different luxury car.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: MAYBACH G 650 LANDAULET — GENEVA MARCH 2017 · PORTAL AXLES + RAISED SUSPENSION FROM THE 4x4² · V12 621 HP · €749,700 · 99 UNITS

scenes.text: Fox News, on the fourth of March twenty thirteen, called it a monster truck, hand-built, with a pickup bed grafted onto the cabin to fit the extra axle. It listed two twenty-one gallon fuel tanks, eight thousand three hundred pounds, and a compressed air system that adjusts tyre pressures remotely. It also said Mercedes expected twenty to thirty units a year, citing Autocar.
scenes.caption: FOX NEWS (4 MAR 2013): 'MONSTER TRUCK' · HAND-BUILT, PICKUP BED GRAFTED ONTO THE CABIN · TWO 21-GAL TANKS · 8,300 LB · 20–30 UNITS/YEAR (CITING AUTOCAR) · FUEL ECONOMY 'NOT DETERMINED'
scenes.chapter: How the press first saw it

scenes.text: Gear Patrol, on the first of March twenty thirteen, quoted around five hundred twenty-six thousand dollars and said Mercedes planned a limited number for the fall. Its tone was jokey, with remarks about torque warping the earth's crust and about compensation. Those are jokes, not facts. The factual part is the spec list: six driven wheels, five locks, thirty-seven inch wheels.
scenes.caption: GEAR PATROL (1 MAR 2013): ~$526,000 · LIMITED NUMBER FOR FALL 2013 · JOKES ABOUT TORQUE AND COMPENSATION (OPINION) · SIX DRIVEN WHEELS, FIVE LOCKS, '37-INCH WHEELS'

scenes.text: Autocar's Greg Kable drove it in February twenty fourteen. He called it a fun thing to drive in the right conditions, remarkably easy to drive, and invincible in the dunes, but a super-exclusive proposition for all but the mega-rich. He found the steering vague on the prototype. He also noted the price was more than three times that of the G 63 AMG.
scenes.caption: AUTOCAR (GREG KABLE, 23 FEB 2014): 'A FUN THING TO DRIVE IN THE RIGHT CONDITIONS' · 'REMARKABLY EASY TO DRIVE' · 'FEELS INVINCIBLE' IN DUNES · STEERING 'VAGUE' (PROTOTYPE) · PRICE '>3×' G 63 AMG

scenes.text: CarAdvice, in April twenty fifteen, called the vehicles Frankenstein utes, five point seven metres long and four tonnes, and said Mercedes had called it quits on one of the wildest road-going machines ever made. By our arithmetic, five point seven metres is about three percent shorter than the fifty-eight seventy-five millimetres on Wikipedia. Press numbers were rounded.
scenes.caption: CARADVICE (13 APR 2015): 'FRANKENSTEIN UTES' · 5.7 M LONG · 4 TONNES · 'CALLED IT QUITS' · 5.7 vs 5.875 M = −3.0% (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: So by 2015, the early press had given us several lengths, weights and prices, and none was a surprise. A product that is built by hand in a few dozen or a hundred copies, with details changing between prototype and production, will produce messy numbers. That is our reading of why the sources differ, not a statement from any of them.
scenes.caption: LENGTH: 5.70 / 5.87 / 5.875 M · WEIGHT: 3.775 / 3.85 / 4.083 T · PRICE: €350K / €450K / €379K → ALL IN DATED SOURCES · REASON = OUR READING

scenes.text: The Drive says the car it covered was delivered new to Japan five years before its November twenty twenty listing, and had only about twenty-five hundred miles in America after arriving the previous year. Motor Authority, a week earlier, said a car on Bring a Trailer had been imported to the United States in September twenty nineteen under the Show and Display exemption.
scenes.caption: THE DRIVE (10 NOV 2020): DELIVERED NEW TO JAPAN ~5 YEARS EARLIER; ~2,500 MI IN US SINCE ARRIVING 'LAST YEAR' · MOTOR AUTHORITY (3 NOV 2020): IMPORTED SEPT 2019, SHOW AND DISPLAY

scenes.text: They probably describe the same car, though neither says so. By our arithmetic, Motor Authority reported a bid of five hundred sixty-seven thousand dollars on the third of November, and The Drive reported a final price of nine hundred one thousand, three hundred thirty-seven a week later. That would be a rise of fifty-nine percent in the final days of the auction.
scenes.query: Bid to sale in a week
scenes.caption: $567,000 (3 NOV 2020) → $901,337 (10 NOV 2020) = +59.0% (OUR ARITHMETIC) · SAME CAR? PROBABLY, NOT STATED IN EITHER SOURCE (OUR READING)

scenes.text: Auctions often move late, but our sources do not discuss that. What they do say is that Motor Authority described used listings from nine hundred seventy-five thousand to one point six million dollars. So in November twenty twenty the market already had asking prices well above the final bid, and the sale closed in the middle of that range.
scenes.caption: MOTOR AUTHORITY: LISTINGS $975,000–$1.6 M · SALE $901,337 = 92% OF THE LOWEST LISTING (OUR ARITHMETIC) · AUCTION-TIMING BEHAVIOUR: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: The import route has its own story. The Drive says G and K Automotive Conversion of Santa Ana made the car road legal. Barrett-Jackson says its lot was federalised by the same company. MercedesBlog says an NHTSA inspection is required until the car is twenty-five years old. So a legal path existed, even though Mercedes never offered the truck new in America.
scenes.caption: THE DRIVE + BARRETT-JACKSON: G&K AUTOMOTIVE CONVERSION, SANTA ANA · MERCEDESBLOG: NHTSA INSPECTION UNTIL 25 YEARS OLD · MBWORLD: NEVER SOLD NEW IN THE U.S.

scenes.text: Owners did not leave it alone. Carscoops describes a Brabus B63S-700 conversion with seven hundred horsepower and seven hundred eight pound-feet, six Brembo brakes and Ohlins shocks. Barrett-Jackson describes a Weistec Engineering car with enhanced turbochargers, downpipes, a modified ECU and a three-inch exhaust. Both fit the because-we-can spirit of the truck.
scenes.caption: CARSCOOPS: BRABUS B63S-700 — 700 HP / 708 LB-FT, BREMBO ×6, OHLINS · BARRETT-JACKSON: WEISTEC — TURBOS, DOWNPIPES, ECU, 3-IN EXHAUST

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, the Brabus car makes thirty-one percent more power than the stock five hundred thirty-six horsepower. The Weistec car's output is not given in the listing we read. So we cannot say how far it went. The sources do not say whether tuning raised or lowered the sale prices, since the cars were not otherwise identical.
scenes.caption: 700 ÷ 536 = +30.6% (OUR ARITHMETIC; BRABUS) · WEISTEC POWER: NOT GIVEN · EFFECT OF TUNING ON PRICE: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: MBWorld, in a piece with no date, says a white 6x6 with nine hundred sixty-five miles fetched one million, four hundred thousand dollars at Barrett-Jackson Scottsdale. The author called it as close to new as you are going to get, and hoped the owner would use the locking differentials every now and again. That is opinion, but it shows how these trucks are viewed.
scenes.caption: MBWORLD (UNDATED): $1.4 MILLION, 965 MI, 2014 CAR, 'FIVE-YEAR-OLD', BARRETT-JACKSON SCOTTSDALE · AUTHOR HOPES OWNER USES LOCKS 'EVERY NOW AND AGAIN' (OPINION) · SALE DATE: NOT STATED

scenes.text: Barrett-Jackson's own copy called it the most effortlessly superior and extravagant off-roader ever to be developed and built by engineers. That is marketing language from an auction house selling the lot, and we mark it as such. Its listing facts are more useful: built at Graz from two thousand thirteen to fifteen, only one hundred produced, seating for four.
scenes.caption: BARRETT-JACKSON: 'MOST EFFORTLESSLY SUPERIOR AND EXTRAVAGANT OFF-ROADER EVER' (MARKETING) · FACTS: BUILT IN GRAZ 2013–2015 · 'ONLY 100' · SEATS FOUR

scenes.text: A timeline in numbers, from our sources. Land one two one prototypes, October two thousand nine. Show car, March twenty thirteen. Sale start, October twenty thirteen. Sold out, February twenty fifteen. Last delivery, May twenty fifteen. By our arithmetic, that is about three years and five months from prototypes to show car, and two years from the show car to sell-out.
scenes.caption: OCT 2009 PROTOTYPES → MAR 2013 SHOW CAR (~3 YR 5 MO) → OCT 2013 SALE START → FEB 2015 SOLD OUT (~23.5 MO FROM 1 MAR 2013) → MAY 2015 LAST DELIVERY (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: And the price timeline: three hundred fifty thousand euros guidance in March twenty thirteen, four hundred fifty thousand quoted in September, three hundred seventy-nine thousand reported as the launch price. Then nine hundred one thousand dollars in November twenty twenty, one million one hundred seventy thousand in May twenty twenty-two, and about six hundred thousand pounds in January twenty twenty-five.
scenes.caption: €350K (MAR 2013 GUIDANCE) → €450K (SEPT 2013, AUTOCAR VIA GOAUTO) → €379K (REPORTED LAUNCH) → $901,337 (NOV 2020) → $1.17 M (MAY 2022, BRABUS) → £602,046 (JAN 2025, CLASSIC VALUER) — MIXED CURRENCIES, DIFFERENT CARS

scenes.text: What does the story show? A military contract created a chassis. A show car in March twenty thirteen was described as having no series plan. By October it was on sale, by February twenty fifteen over a hundred were built and sold out, and by twenty twenty its resale price had passed its launch price. Each step is in a dated source.
scenes.caption: 2007–2009 ARMY CONTRACT/PROTOTYPES → MAR 2013 SHOW CAR → OCT 2013 SALES → FEB 2015 SOLD OUT, 100+ BUILT → NOV 2020 $901,337 USED (EACH STEP DATED ABOVE)

scenes.text: What the story does not show is why. Our sources do not contain a Mercedes document explaining the decision to sell the show car, the size of the run, or the price. McCarthy's remark that if people want one, they will make them one is the closest thing, and it is the remark of a regional spokesman, not the board.
scenes.caption: WHY MERCEDES SOLD THE SHOW CAR / RUN SIZE / PRICE: NOT IN OUR SOURCES · CLOSEST: McCARTHY — 'IF PEOPLE WANT ONE, THEY WILL MAKE THEM ONE' (REGIONAL SPOKESMAN)

scenes.text: What is missing. The exact build count. A Mercedes statement on the reasons for the price changes. Who the first customers were, beyond the Malaysian and South African orders. And the currency of the army contract. If you know any of these from a primary document, tell us in the comments.
scenes.caption: NOT IN OUR SOURCES: EXACT BUILD COUNT · MERCEDES REASONS FOR PRICE CHANGES · FIRST CUSTOMER LIST · CURRENCY OF THE ARMY CONTRACT
scenes.chapter: What our sources do not say

scenes.text: Do you think a military chassis dressed in diamond-quilted leather makes sense, or is it the best kind of excess? Tell us in the comments.
